analysis.title: US Midterms : Blunami !
key_insights: Democrats regained control of the House and the Senate in the 2026 midterms. The Senate count so far is six seat gains and an expected majority of at least 54 seats. Not all results were in at publication.
The wave reached historically Republican states including Texas, South Carolina and Kansas (a first since 1932). The report calls it the most stinging defeat for a sitting president since 1946.

The report attributes the result to voter frustration over inflation, Trump's unpopularity, his immigration policy, attacks on institutions and the war against Iran. It says the trade war and the Iran military campaign contributed to higher inflation. Democrats campaigned on purchasing power.

Trump's veto power and political tensions are expected to block Democratic legislation. Pressure from Republicans ahead of the 2028 presidential election should dissuade Trump from granting major wins. Democratic committees of inquiry into allegations that Trump enriched himself should strain relations further.

The base case is institutional deadlock with no major progress on fiscal policy. The report says this should limit the widening of the budget deficit and ease one source of upward pressure on US Treasury yields.

The risk to the base case is a Senate result of up to 57 Democratic seats under some projections. Around ten Republican defectors would then suffice to reach the two-thirds majority needed to override a veto or impeach the president. The report calls this scenario unlikely at this stage.

The report says the Texas governor race mattered most for markets. Republican G. Abbott, a leading advocate of data centre development, lost to Democrat G. Hinojosa, who made regulation of tech giants her main campaign issue. Texas accounts for nearly a third of US data centre capacity available or under construction. Polls had Abbott as the favourite until the night of the vote.

Referendums and local votes covering an area with 170 of the 300 GW of planned US data centre capacity adopted around twenty restrictive measures to curb new data centres. These results are provisional.

The initial market reaction was a Nasdaq fall of 2% and a Kospi fall of 4%. Both indices then recovered gradually and had returned to equilibrium by the morning after. Investors are hoping the anti-AI rhetoric was a campaign stance. Hinojosa's programme calls for rules to protect rights and limit extra costs for households, not a total ban.

The report expects data centre regulation uncertainty to persist in the short term while tech companies negotiate with new local authorities. It expects investors to regain risk appetite as visibility improves, and equity indices to resume their rise.

The report cites history: the year after midterms that leave power shared between the two parties has been one of the best periods for equities. It also cites solid global growth, exceptional corporate earnings and valuations back at particularly attractive levels. It stays positive on equities while diversifying across sectors, regions and into bonds, to use the decorrelation between the two asset classes.

sector_views.rationale: Positive on equities because of favourable post-midterm seasonality, solid global growth, exceptional corporate earnings and attractive valuations. The report also recommends diversifying across sectors and regions.
The report recommends diversifying into bonds to use the decorrelation between bonds and equities. It says fiscal deadlock should limit deficit widening and ease upward pressure on Treasury yields.

earnings_insights: The report describes corporate earnings as exceptional and cites them as one reason to stay positive on equities. It gives no specific figures.

macro_indicators.reading: Widening expected to be limited by institutional deadlock
macro_indicators.interpretation: Little fiscal policy progress should limit deficit expansion and ease upward pressure on US sovereign bond yields.
Supports the report's positive stance on equities.

Data centre regulation uncertainty could weigh on markets in the short term.

If Democrats prove less pragmatic than investors hope, anti-AI rhetoric could turn into policy.

tension_points.bull_case: Hinojosa's programme does not call for a total ban on data centres, only rules to safeguard rights and limit extra household costs. Investors hope the anti-AI rhetoric was a campaign stance and that Democrats will be pragmatic once in power. Indices recovered their losses by the next morning.
tension_points.bear_case: Texas has nearly a third of US data centre capacity. Around twenty restrictive measures were adopted across areas holding 170 of 300 GW of planned capacity. The report says uncertainty is likely to persist in the short term and could weigh on markets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Negotiations between tech companies and the new local authorities failing to produce agreements.

tension_points.bull_case: With deadlock, fiscal policy makes no major progress, the deficit widens less and upward pressure on yields eases.
tension_points.bear_case: If Democrats win up to 57 Senate seats, around ten Republican defectors could give the two-thirds majority needed to override a veto or impeach the president.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A final Senate result of up to 57 Democratic seats.
